start_here: Say to your AI: "Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others", with {"records":[],"email":"reader@example.com","consent":true,"course":{"id":"sample-course","public_origin":"https://example.com/","checkout_url":"https://example.com/#pricing","from":"Coach <coach@example.com>","mailing_address":"1 Example Street, Example City, CA 90000","consent_text":"Send me three lessons by email.","consent_version":"1","lessons":[{"delay_hours":0,"subject":"First lesson" .... It runs tool:sign-someone-up-for-an-email-course and answers {"status":"enrolled","already_enrolled":false}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps nothing and reads no store. Your AI reads the rows it works over from your lists and hands them in (records); the answer holds the rows to keep for your AI to write.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others", and give it email; consent; course; provider.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:sign-someone-up-for-an-email-course and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, checkout_url, from, mailing_address, consent_text, consent_version and 2 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines } where every lesson carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} and the first has delay_hours 0), source (where they signed up, optional) records (the person's rows listed in its schema, read from their store) and provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is; region too when that row asks for one). Nothing is sent without consent, a sender and a mailing address. Works out the consent row with its words, version, time and source and each later lesson's queue row at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons sends them), and answers them in keep for the caller to write; nothing is kept here; sends lesson 1 with List-Unsubscribe headers; signing up again sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.
4. It keeps nothing and has no records door: it works over the rows you hand in (records) and answers the rows to keep (keep), each with the row it expected, for your AI to write to your store.
